description: The typed edge schema for the multi-relational memory plane. Changing any field or enum invalidates all annotated edges and requires a version bump.

supports.definition: One record provides evidence, refinement, elaboration, or repetition for another. Following one reinforces or is consistent with the other.
includes: One is a specific instance of the other
One provides rationale for the other
Both say the same thing differently
One adds detail without changing the other's meaning

contradicts.definition: Following both records is impossible; one forbids what the other requires, or they specify incompatible values for the same thing.
includes: Direct negation ('must use X' vs 'must not use X')
Scope conflicts that make both unfollowable simultaneously
excludes: records about different topics that merely coexist

supersedes.definition: One record replaces another due to a version change, decision reversal, or time passage. The superseded record is no longer intended to be followed.
supersedes.direction_semantics: src supersedes dst (dst is the old record, src is the new)
includes: Version updates ('use v15' replaced by 'use v16')
Policy reversals ('allow X' replaced by 'no longer allow X')
Scope narrowing that effectively replaces the old rule
excludes: records that complement each other without replacing

unrelated.definition: The two records talk about different aspects, systems, or concerns. Following one has no bearing on the other.
includes: Records at different abstraction levels with no shared constraint

abstain.definition: Cannot determine the relationship; requires domain knowledge, broader context, or a judgement call not available to the annotator.
abstain.usage: Use sparingly; high abstain rate signals ontology ambiguity

status.description: annotation output is always proposed; confirmation is a separate event

direction.description: only required when type=supersedes; src supersedes dst

evidence_span.description: key phrase from the pair that supports this classification

provenance.requirement: Every edge must be traceable to: (1) the annotator who created it (source field), (2) the annotation guide version used, (3) the exact record texts forming the pair (via src/dst node ids).
